example_hts_shield./hts/psi/note: Psi recomputed with the critical-state static field and the same pickup mode, at the step with the largest drive scale; the baseline is the ideal (Meissner) model at drive scale 1, so relative_change divides by the peak scale. Psi(t) of every step is in `steps`

example_hts_shield./pickup/losses/surfaces/shield/note: R_eff = R_s(f) * Gamma; Q = 2 pi f L_p / R_eff
example_hts_shield./pickup/port_capacitance/checks/dirichle: rigorous (Dirichlet principle, exact for the discrete problems): C_gap_port_region <= C_gap + (C_A_to_ground + C_B_to_ground)/4. The stronger C_gap >= C_gap_port_region is NOT proven; it is observed on every case run so far, with C_gap/C_region falling towards 1 as the gap grows relative to the electrode spacing (1.02 at the widest gap tested, 5.6 at the narrowest), but the bound above is the only guaranteed one.
example_hts_shield./pickup/port_capacitance/note: C_gap_port_region_F: the electrostatic capacitance of the gap region alone, with natural (insulating) conditions on the faces open to the cavity -- no fringing. C_gap_F: the same two terminal faces driven at V = +-1/2 on the whole domain, with the rest of their own conductor body insulating (n.D = 0) and every other conductor floating -- this adds the fringing field at the two mouths of the gap. The only rigorous relation between them is the Dirichlet bound in checks/dirichlet_bound; neither is a proven bound on the other. Both are lumped-element estimates: the body is electrically continuous around the port, so a capacitance across the readout exists only in the lumped model. f = 1/(2 pi sqrt(L_p C_gap)) is an ESTIMATE of the first self-resonance, not a bound in either direction: C_gap is only the gap's share of the structure's capacitance (which pushes the estimate up), while a distributed line resonates at (pi/2) / (2 pi sqrt(L C_total)) (which pushes the true pole up). The estimate exceeds the first pole only while C_gap/C_total < (2/pi)^2 = 0.405; it is 0.09 and 0.16 for the shipped solenoid and core templates, which is why it came out high there. The pole of L(omega) in a full-wave sweep (design key 'fullwave') is the reference for distributed structures.
example_hts_shield./warnings/0: superconductor 'shield': the peak surface field 3.4441 T is at a sharp corner (r = 0.47, z = 0.6 m) where the field is singular and grows under mesh refinement; away from such corners the peak is 1.62203 T (superconductor_surface_regular_T). Round the corner (fillet) for a meaningful peak field.
example_hts_shield./warnings/1: critical-state analysis: 'conductor' (normal metal) regions carry no eddy currents in the time-dependent solve, so the reported dissipation is the HTS loss alone

example_pickup_capacitance./checks/0/name: Newton's third law: total axial force on all bodies
example_pickup_capacitance./coupling/note: g = Psi^2/(L_p W R^2) in natural units, R = device outer radius
example_pickup_capacitance./electrostatics/checks/floating_solve/no: body 0 at 1 V, every other conductor floating at zero net charge; the potentials must match -C_FF^{-1} C_F0 from the Maxwell matrix
example_pickup_capacitance./electrostatics/checks/what_each_check_t: ALGEBRAIC IDENTITIES of the discrete system -- they verify the assembly and the linear solves, not the discretization: symmetry_* (the matrix is built from reactions, not from a symmetrized Schur complement), energy_* and energy_superposition (the same quadratic form reassembled by quadrature), floating_solve (the exact matrix reduction) and exterior_monopole_* (1^T K phi = eps_out p_0 identically, so the sum of the reaction charges equals 4 pi eps_out Rb a_0 up to the solver residual and the geometric error of the boundary arc). DISCRETIZATION CHECKS -- they converge under h/p refinement and are the ones to read: charge_gauss_* (reactions against the strong surface integral of eps E.n over the conductors) and exterior_flux_* (the net charge from the strong flux -int eps grad(phi).n dA over the outer sphere, which the weakly imposed DtN map only reproduces in the limit).
example_pickup_capacitance./electrostatics/convention: Maxwell matrix: C(i, j) = Q_i for V_j = 1 V and every other conductor at 0 V; ground is infinity (open) or the outer sphere (grounded). C_to_ground = row sum. The pairwise mutual capacitance is -C(i, j) (the lumped capacitor of the equivalent network, i.e. with the other conductors grounded); C_mutual_others_floating_F instead holds the other conductors at zero net charge (an exact reduction of the matrix).

The stronger C_gap >= C_gap_port_region is NOT proven; it is observed on every case run so far, with C_gap/C_region falling towards 1 as the gap grows relative to the electrode spacing (1.02 at the widest gap tested, 5.6 at the narrowest), but the bound above is the only guaranteed one.
template_solenoid./pickup/port_capacitance/note: C_gap_port_region_F: the electrostatic capacitance of the gap region alone, with natural (insulating) conditions on the faces open to the cavity -- no fringing. C_gap_F: the same two terminal faces driven at V = +-1/2 on the whole domain, with the rest of their own conductor body insulating (n.D = 0) and every other conductor floating -- this adds the fringing field at the two mouths of the gap. The only rigorous relation between them is the Dirichlet bound in checks/dirichlet_bound; neither is a proven bound on the other. Both are lumped-element estimates: the body is electrically continuous around the port, so a capacitance across the readout exists only in the lumped model. f = 1/(2 pi sqrt(L_p C_gap)) is an ESTIMATE of the first self-resonance, not a bound in either direction: C_gap is only the gap's share of the structure's capacitance (which pushes the estimate up), while a distributed line resonates at (pi/2) / (2 pi sqrt(L C_total)) (which pushes the true pole up). The estimate exceeds the first pole only while C_gap/C_total < (2/pi)^2 = 0.405; it is 0.09 and 0.16 for the shipped solenoid and core templates, which is why it came out high there. The pole of L(omega) in a full-wave sweep (design key 'fullwave') is the reference for distributed structures.
